observation_summary: The chi-square test statistic calculation was incorrect because it failed to account for cases where the sum of observed counts does not equal the sum of expected counts, leading to inaccurate results.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves rewriting the computational logic of the chi-square statistic calculation. It introduces a rescaling step to ensure the sum of expected values matches the sum of observed values when they differ. This is a procedural correction to the mathematical algorithm used to compute the statistic, rather than a simple guard (Checking) or a single value initialization (Assignment/Initialization).
evidence_used: The bug report states that the calculation is only correct if sum(observed) == sum(expected) and that rescaling is required otherwise.
The fix diff shows the addition of logic to calculate sums and a conditional rescaling factor applied to the computation of the chi-square statistic.
The fix modifies the core loop that computes the sumSq variable, which is the heart of the chi-square algorithm.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds a conditional check (if rescale), the primary purpose is to modify the mathematical formula used for the calculation, not just to validate input parameters.
The fix involves more than just initializing a variable; it changes the entire computational procedure for the chi-square statistic.
